claims.text: Structural and chemical stability is governed by a dynamic equilibrium between surface segregation and bulk diffusion.
Nanoparticle composition modulates the equilibrium between surface segregation and bulk diffusion.
Operating temperature modulates the equilibrium between surface segregation and bulk diffusion.
The as-synthesized nanoparticles have a uniform composition.
The as-synthesized nanoparticles are crystalline solid solutions.
The catalytic experiment is conducted at 873 K in hydrogen.
The thermoelectric experiment is conducted at 673 K in vacuum.
The specimens are heated at 5 K/min and held for 2 hours.
Noble metals undergo surface segregation during service.
Alloying elements undergo bulk diffusion during service.
After 2 hours of catalytic operation, the lattice parameter increases by 20% relative to the as-synthesized state.
After 2 hours of catalytic operation, the surface noble-metal concentration decreases by 15% relative to the as-synthesized state.
After 2 hours of thermoelectric operation, the lattice parameter decreases by 10% relative to the as-synthesized state.
After 2 hours of thermoelectric operation, the surface noble-metal concentration increases by 5% relative to the as-synthesized state.
The as-synthesized baseline lattice parameter is 0.4 nm.
The as-synthesized baseline surface noble-metal concentration is 20%.
The hypothesis does not apply when composition deviates by more than 10% from near-equiatomic stoichiometry.
The hypothesis is bounded to 773–1173 K for catalytic operation and 473–1923 K for thermoelectric operation.
Nanoparticle size and shape may influence the proposed dynamic equilibrium.

contradictions.description: The mediator states that noble metals undergo surface segregation, ordinarily implying surface enrichment, whereas catalytic operation is predicted to decrease surface noble-metal concentration by 15%; no mechanism is supplied to reconcile this direction.
